segments.t: Around nine o'clock, the courtyard grows peaceful again as Qing and Chen stack clean white teacups inside Room Nine while Teacher Song closes the walnut piano lid gently. Listen first.
一个杯子也没磕破，一根保险丝也没烧断，还有二十四位开心的邻居。
老陈，你在笑呢！我在灯光底下看得清清楚楚！
小晴，那准是磨砂玻璃灯罩晃了眼。
小晴，今晚你合上那本大纸登记本以前……
宋老师，四号房一切都好吗？门铃是不是又响了两声？
我倒很喜欢那两声铃响——下个星期四号房还空着吗？
等等——宋老师，您想在我们这儿续住吗？！
要是你们留我，我想再住两个星期——每个星期五都来弹琴配茶！
宋老师，只要您愿意，四号房随时都是您的。
用铅笔记在这儿啦！小美和周经理一定会高兴坏了！
对了，刚才邮递员往门口信箱里塞了一张厚厚的外国明信片。
星期五晚上还有信？我们快拿到前台去看看！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
一个杯子也没磕破，一根保险丝也没烧断，还有二十四位开心的邻居。

'Not one chipped cup, zero blown fuses, and twenty-four happy neighbours.' Repeating "yi... ye mei...", "not even a single...", lets Chen tally his proud handyman report card. Notice "baoxiansi" for an electrical fuse: literally "safety wire".
老陈，你在笑呢！我在灯光底下看得清清楚楚！
'You are smiling, Chen! I saw it clearly under the lamp!' Watch two-syllable "qingchu", "clear", double syllable by syllable into "qingqingchuchu"—turning "clearly" into "plain as day".
小晴，那准是磨砂玻璃灯罩晃了眼。
'Must be a trick of the frosted glass, Qing.' "Zhun shi" is a breezy, colloquial way to say "must be", and "mosha boli" literally describes frosted glass as "sand-rubbed glass".
小晴，今晚你合上那本大纸登记本以前……

'Qing, before you close the big paper reservation book tonight...' Mandarin chooses different "close" words by shape: "guan" shuts a door, while "heshang"—"bring together"—closes a book or a piano lid. Notice "yiqian", "before", sits at the very end.
宋老师，四号房一切都好吗？门铃是不是又响了两声？

'Is everything all right in Room Four, Teacher Song? Did the buzzer ring twice again?' "Shibushi", literally "is-not-is", lets Qing check a hunch she already suspects is true—that quirky double ring in Room Four.
我倒很喜欢那两声铃响——下个星期四号房还空着吗？
'I have grown quite fond of that double ring—is Room Four free next week?' Slipping tiny "dao" right after "I" adds a charming twist: "far from minding it, I actually like it!".
等等——宋老师，您想在我们这儿续住吗？！
'Wait—you want to extend your stay with us, Teacher Song?!' "Xuzhu" packs "continue" and "stay" into two neat front-desk syllables you can use at any inn when you want extra nights.
要是你们留我，我想再住两个星期——每个星期五都来弹琴配茶！

'Two more weeks, if you will have me—and I will play every Friday for tea!' Notice "zai zhu liang ge xingqi" for "stay two more weeks": "zai" sits in front of the action rather than inside the number phrase.
宋老师，只要您愿意，四号房随时都是您的。
'Room Four belongs to you as long as you want it, Teacher Song.' "Zhiyao", "only need", opens warm "as long as" promises, and "nin de" at the end turns polite "you" into "yours".
用铅笔记在这儿啦！小美和周经理一定会高兴坏了！

'Written in pencil right here! Mei and Manager Zhou will be thrilled!' Fun twist: tacking "-huai le", literally "broken", onto "happy" means "thrilled to bits"—the exact same playful intensifier turns "hungry" into "starving"!
对了，刚才邮递员往门口信箱里塞了一张厚厚的外国明信片。

'Oh, by the way, the postman slipped a thick foreign postcard into the gate box.' "Dui le!"—literally "Right!"—is Mandarin's effortless pivot for "Oh, by the way!", and "mingxinpians" means "open-letter card" since a postcard travels without an envelope.
星期五晚上还有信？我们快拿到前台去看看！

'Evening mail on a Friday? Let us take it to the front desk and look!' "Qiantai", "front-stage" or "front-counter", is the universal word for a hotel front desk, and quick "kankan" keeps the invitation light and eager.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
一个杯子也没磕破，一根保险丝也没烧断，还有二十四位开心的邻居。
老陈，你在笑呢！我在灯光底下看得清清楚楚！
小晴，那准是磨砂玻璃灯罩晃了眼。
小晴，今晚你合上那本大纸登记本以前……
宋老师，四号房一切都好吗？门铃是不是又响了两声？
我倒很喜欢那两声铃响——下个星期四号房还空着吗？

要是你们留我，我想再住两个星期——每个星期五都来弹琴配茶！
宋老师，只要您愿意，四号房随时都是您的。
用铅笔记在这儿啦！小美和周经理一定会高兴坏了！
对了，刚才邮递员往门口信箱里塞了一张厚厚的外国明信片。
星期五晚上还有信？我们快拿到前台去看看！
Teacher Song stays on as Room Nine's Friday pianist, and a late postcard waits in the gate mailbox for our final scene of Season 2! See you next time.
